description: Normative global 1.5°C pathway reaching net zero CO2 around 2050; MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM 2.0.
pathwayDescription:
The Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) develops reference climate transition and physical risk scenarios to support financial institutions, regulators, and policymakers in assessing climate-related financial risks. These scenarios provide globally consistent projections of emissions, energy systems, and macroeconomic trends under varying policy and temperature pathways. Their Net Zero 2050, MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM 2.0-M-R12 (NZ2050 MESSAGE) Scenario is a normative, high-ambition global pathway in which the world achieves net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2070, consistent with limiting warming to below 1.5°C. It assumes immediate and coordinated global policy action, rapid decarbonization across all sectors, and large-scale deployment of clean energy and negative-emission technologies.

The NZ2050 GCAM pathway ensures net-zero CO₂ emissions by 2070, with residual non-CO₂ gases offset through negative-emission technologies such as bioenergy with carbon capture and sequestration (BECCS) and direct air capture (DAC). This results in 1.5°C of cumulative warming in 2100. Fossil fuel use declines by roughly 90% by mid-century, with unabated coal nearly eliminated by 2040 and sharp reductions in oil and gas. Global energy demand stabilizes as efficiency gains and electrification offset growth in activity.

NZ2050 represents the most ambitious pathway in the NGFS scenario set. NZ2050 builds on existing and announced policies but introduces stringent emissions limits and rapid technology innovation. Note that all NGFS scenarios are produced using three different Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs): REMIND-MAgPIE, MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM, and GCAM. These IAMs share the common assumptions that define each scenario, but may offer different projections based on underlying model structure. Technical users may wish to consult NGFS documentation to determine if a specific IAM best fits their applications.

coreDrivers.policies: Carbon price: the shadow carbon price reaches 257 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030 and 461 in 2050, the main lever moving investment and dispatch away from fossil fuels.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: Temperature and net-zero constraint: 1.5°C with global net zero CO2 around 2050, plus national net-zero targets (Table 37) met on time. MESSAGE applies net-zero GHG constraints by its 12 regions and approximates CO2-only targets with a 10-year-lagged GHG target.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: MESSAGE minimises total system cost from investment, O&M and fuel costs. Exogenous declines (North America solar PV 853 to 374 US$2010/kW, 2020-2050) favour renewables, while cheap CCS keeps gas in the mix: wind and solar reach 83% of 2050 generation (Current Policies 31%). With carbon at 461 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, the cost ranking tilts further to low-carbon options.
coreDrivers.investmentChange: Low-carbon power investment moves from 1.11% of GDP (MER) in 2020 to 0.65% in 2050, a decrease of 42%. MESSAGE's GDP grows faster than its power investment, so the share falls even where low-carbon investment rises in absolute terms.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Shared SSP2 v3.0 population and GDP drive energy and material demand: 9.59 billion people in 2050 and GDP (MER) growing 3.82%/yr over 2020-2050. The assumptions are common to all NGFS scenarios; GDP differs from Current Policies only through transition costs (-1.23% in 2050).
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: Limited carbon dioxide removal: MESSAGE constrains BECCS availability by 2050, forcing deeper gross cuts and higher carbon prices (461 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050; total CCS 4755 Mt CO2/yr). It is a technology-availability limit, not a cost, policy or target, so no other driver fits.

dependencies.dependency_description: Grid decarbonisation in Net Zero 2050 (MESSAGE) rests on the carbon price (257 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030, 461 in 2050). It lifts wind and solar from 9% of generation in 2020 to 83% in 2050 and cuts coal capacity to 13% of its 2020 level by 2040.

Power investment averages 1412 bn US$2010/yr over 2025-2050 (1.81x Current Policies), including 529 bn/yr for grids, and must be financed. A 2050 carbon price of 461 US$2010/tCO2 erodes unabated fossil plant profitability.

With wind and solar at 83% of 2050 generation, grids, storage and flexibility must absorb variable output. MESSAGE uses reliability coefficients and reaches 6784 GW of storage by 2050. Grid investment averages 529 bn US$2010/yr (2025-2050). No hourly dispatch is reported, so curtailment cannot be checked.

Power CCS captures 35 Mt CO2/yr in 2050 (6 Mt from bioenergy), so the pathway needs CCS at commercial scale; CCS cost differences between models drive large gaps in fossil generation. Storage of 6784 GW in 2050 relies on continued storage cost declines.

MESSAGE uses regional renewable potentials by quality and GLOBIOM biomass limited by food land. Power BECCS reaches 6 Mt CO2/yr and primary biomass 69 EJ in 2050, so land limits the negative-emission part of the power transition. Wind and solar at 83% of 233 EJ draw on the regional potentials.

Steel decarbonisation in Net Zero 2050 (MESSAGE) is steered only through economy-wide carbon pricing (461 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050) and emissions constraints; no steel-specific industrial policy is described. Steel emissions change by -36% over 2020-2050.

At 461 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, fossil ironmaking costs more, favouring electricity (6.1 EJ) and hydrogen (0.0 EJ) in steel in 2050. No steel investment or unit-cost data are reported, so financing needs cannot be quantified.
MESSAGEix-Materials tracks recyclable steel scrap endogenously, so scrap availability limits secondary steelmaking in Net Zero 2050 (MESSAGE); scrap volumes are not reported.

byMetric.scopeLimitations: Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Derived Mt CO2 per EJ generated (1 EJ = 277.8 TWh). Scope 1 CO2 only; denominator is gross generation incl. CCS and bioenergy plants.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. CO2 only, Scope 1 (power-plant combustion, net of CCS); may include the electricity share of CHP.

Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Storage: one aggregate figure (Capacity|Electricity|Storage, GW) covering all storage; the source does not split it into battery, pumped hydro or hydrogen. Solar = PV + CSP; wind = onshore + offshore; CCS and non-CCS variants reported separately.

Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Gross secondary electricity (EJ/yr) by technology incl. CHP electricity; CCS and non-CCS variants reported. MESSAGE also reports transmission losses.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Derived generation shares; storage excluded (not a generating technology).
Overnight capital cost per kW by technology (geothermal, hydro, nuclear, solar PV, wind only; World aggregate 0, regional values only). No O&M, fuel or LCOE values.
